title: An agent shops with a Visa card: actors and protocol boundaries
caption: Visa Intelligent Commerce holds the consumer's consent, the agent-specific token and the transaction confirmations. TAP carries the agent's signatures to the merchant: agent-browser-auth while browsing, agent-payer-auth at checkout with two signed body objects. The CDN verifies header signatures against Visa's key store; the merchant verifies the body objects; card authorization runs on ordinary card rails outside TAP. The JWKS that the specification named until October 2026 held one RSA sandbox key on 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-19, so the specification's example keys cannot be resolved there.
alt: Flowchart. The consumer chats with the AI agent and authenticates a Payment Instruction with a passkey for Visa Intelligent Commerce. The agent enrolls the card, creates the instruction, retrieves credentials and later sends a confirmation to Visa Intelligent Commerce. The agent sends browsing requests tagged agent-browser-auth and a checkout request tagged agent-payer-auth with the agenticConsumer and agenticPaymentContainer objects to the merchant's CDN. The CDN fetches the key by keyid from Visa's key store, whose URL the specification no longer names, a dashed line, and forwards verified requests to the merchant website. The merchant verifies the body objects and the credential hash, then sends a card authorization to the acquirer, Visa network and issuer, which sits outside TAP.

sourceOfTruth.label: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol specification (unversioned, read 2026-10-11, rechecked 2026-10-19)
